README.md.overview: The English user guide for agm, a Rust control panel that sits beside herdr/herdr-core and meters tokens, context fill and subscription quota across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and agy. It defines the vocabulary (inbox, daemon, rotation, handoff, budgets) that the rest of the tour assumes, so it is the first stop for newcomers.

sections.title: Pitch and scope
sections.explanation: The title, feature bullets and platform note explain what agm tracks: tokens, context fullness, quota windows, an inbox of blocked agents and inter-agent messages. It also states the intervention features (budgets, rotation, handoff) and that the current version is 0.4.0.

sections.title: Install and quick start
sections.explanation: Sections 1 and 2 cover installing the single binary and getting a first useful output within a minute. The README stresses there is no runtime dependency because the tool is one Rust executable.

sections.title: How agm works
sections.explanation: Explains the core design: agm is installed once per machine and reads the logs each tool already writes (JSONL for Claude and Codex, SQLite for OpenCode, transcripts for agy) into ~/.agmag/agm.db. The ASCII diagram and per-tool table show what, if anything, each agent needs to configure, such as the optional `agm hook install` for Claude quota.

sections.title: Daemon, dashboard and agent integration
sections.explanation: Describes the background daemon, the dashboard, when to prefer hc versus agm, and how agents themselves can use agm, including the MCP server and BRANCHES.md coordination. This maps to the later ingestion, daemon and MCP tour steps.

sections.title: Command reference
sections.explanation: A table of every subcommand and its flags. It is a handy index to the `Cmd` enum in src/main.rs and notes safety rules, for example kill/interrupt for Codex and Claude always require a typed y, and spawn exits with code 3 when a brief is not delivered.

sections.title: Statistics, budgets and configuration
sections.explanation: Covers token statistics over time, budgets/policy/rotation, and the providers.toml configuration. The configuration part corresponds to the Config, Policy and Price types in src/config.rs.

sections.title: Safety, limits and development
sections.explanation: Documents data safety, known limitations and development notes (build and test). Read it before changing behavior that touches kill, rotate or the database.

CHANGELOG.md.overview: Keep-a-Changelog style history of agm from 0.1.0 to 0.4.0, written in Vietnamese. It records the new features and fixes per version, so it is the quickest way to see how the CLI, MCP server and rotation logic evolved.

sections.title: Unreleased fix
sections.explanation: The unreleased entry fixes `agm spawn` on Windows when the fallback path cannot deliver the template brief. The CLI now exits with code 3 instead of reporting success, MCP returns an error and rotation marks needs_attention, which matches the latest commit.

sections.title: 0.4.0 MCP and branch locking
sections.explanation: 0.4.0 added `agm mcp` (stdio JSON-RPC server with 7 tools and no kill/interrupt tools) and `agm branch get|set` with a lock under .agents/.runtime/locks plus atomic temp-file rename. The fixes list shows careful concurrency work: lock owner ids, retries on Windows file-busy codes, and SQLite lock handling for concurrent processes.

sections.title: 0.3.x releases
sections.explanation: The 0.3 series adds and changes features around quota polling, spawn, rotation and reporting, with fixes after each. Skim it for the reasoning behind current defaults.

sections.title: 0.2.0 and 0.1.0
sections.explanation: Earliest releases establishing the scan, ls, cost and quota basics that the model and parser layers still serve.

Cargo.toml.overview: Cargo manifest for the agmag crate (version 0.4.0, Rust edition 2024) that builds the `agm` binary. It lists the dependencies that shape the architecture: clap for the CLI, rusqlite (bundled SQLite) for storage, serde/serde_json/toml for data, comfy-table for output.

sections.title: Package metadata
sections.explanation: Names the crate agmag at 0.4.0 using edition 2024. The edition matters because the code relies on let-chains (`if let ... && ...`).

sections.title: Runtime dependencies
sections.explanation: anyhow and thiserror cover error handling; clap with derive builds the command tree; rusqlite with the bundled feature compiles SQLite in so no system library is needed; walkdir finds log files; sysinfo (trimmed features) powers `agm sys`; unicode-width and unicode-segmentation help table and TUI layout.

sections.title: Platform-specific dependencies
sections.explanation: windows-sys and libc are used only to read the terminal pane size for `agm tui`, selected per target with cfg tables.

sections.title: Dev dependencies and binary
sections.explanation: tempfile supports integration tests. The [[bin]] entry names the executable `agm` and points at src/main.rs, while the library target is implicit from src/lib.rs.

src/lib.rs.overview: The library root of the crate. It only declares modules, so integration tests in tests/ and the binary in main.rs share the same code through `agmag::...`.

sections.title: Module declarations
sections.explanation: Each `pub mod` exposes one subsystem: model and config (domain and settings), parse/ingest/opencode/agy (reading logs), store (SQLite), report and dashboard (output), policy/rotation/daemon/actions (control), and mcp/hc/git/launch (integration with other tools). Making them public is what lets tests import internals, and main.rs only adds `mod ops` and `mod tui` privately.

src/main.rs.overview: Entry point of the `agm` binary. It defines the clap command tree, resolves the data directory, optionally scans logs, then dispatches each subcommand to ops.rs, the report/store modules or the TUI. It also holds the table-printing helpers for ls, cost and quota.

sections.title: Imports and module wiring
sections.explanation: Pulls in clap, comfy-table and the library crate `agmag`. Only `ops` and `tui` are declared as modules here; everything else comes from the shared library.

sections.title: CLI definition (Cli and Cmd)
sections.explanation: `Cli` carries the global `--json` flag and a `Cmd` enum with one variant per subcommand (scan, ls, cost, quota, daemon, send, spawn, kill, rotate, budget, mcp, tui...). Doc comments on variants become the clap help text, so the enum doubles as documentation.

sections.title: Nested subcommands and helpers
sections.explanation: BranchCmd, BudgetCmd and HookCmd model the second-level commands. `parse_pair` validates KEY=VALUE arguments, and SCAN_DAYS/DAY_MS set the default scan window of seven days.

sections.title: Home, roots and main
sections.explanation: `agm_home` honors AGM_HOME or falls back to ~/.agmag, and `roots` allows overriding log directories by environment variable, which is helpful for tests. `main` handles two commands that must not need a database (hook statusline and sys) before calling `run`, then maps errors to exit codes via `actions::exit_code`.

sections.title: run: scanning and dispatch
sections.explanation: `run` opens the store, loads config lazily (so commands like `policy off` or `kill` still work with a broken providers.toml), computes how far back to scan for view commands, ingests, and then matches on `cli.cmd`. Mutating commands delegate to ops functions, while read commands call report builders and print functions.

sections.title: Date parsing and scan
sections.explanation: `parse_local_date_ms` converts a local YYYY-MM-DD to epoch milliseconds, using SQLite to learn the UTC offset. `scan` ingests every source and reports a failure of a single source (OpenCode, agy) without aborting the others.

sections.title: Output helpers
sections.explanation: Functions that render terminals, sessions, cost tables (with a separate bold SUM row), quota windows and the summary report. `emit` chooses JSON or human output, and JSON is automatic when stdout is not a TTY.

sections.title: Unit tests
sections.explanation: Tests for quota rendering helpers such as stale-row marking, placed in the same file to access private functions.

src/ops.rs.overview: Implementations of the v1 CLI commands that need side effects: branch files, daemon loop, messages and inbox, spawning and stopping agents, rotation, budgets, linking and the Claude statusline hook. main.rs stays a thin dispatcher while this file does the work, mostly by calling the `actions`, `rotation`, `policy` and `store` modules.

sections.title: Caller detection
sections.explanation: `hc_terminal` reads HC_TERMINAL_ID. `caller` decides whether the actor is a user or an agent, failing closed to agent when unsure, and asks a y/N question on stderr for dangerous actions. Accepted answers include the Vietnamese word for yes.

sections.title: Branch commands
sections.explanation: `branch_get` and `branch_set` wrap the locked, atomic BRANCHES.md editing described in the CHANGELOG for 0.4.0.

sections.title: Daemon replay and loop
sections.explanation: `daemon_replay` feeds saved hc events into the store for debugging. `daemon_loop` starts a background thread that keeps `hc events --json` running (restarting after 5 s) and sends lines through an mpsc channel. The main loop waits for events with recv_timeout, and every interval it drains events and runs scanning, terminal linking, policy and rotation, each reported independently so one failing step does not stop the rest.

sections.title: Messages and inbox
sections.explanation: `send`, `inbox` and `reply` give a thin layer over the store for agent-to-agent and agent-to-user messaging.

sections.title: Spawn, stop and rotate
sections.explanation: `spawn` prints the new terminal's address even on BriefUndelivered so scripts know a worker runs, then returns the error to give exit code 3. `stop` forces a typed confirmation for anything except OpenCode, because `--yes` could be added by an agent. `rotate` queues OpenCode workers or managed Claude/Codex sessions and never kills the old session for the latter.

sections.title: Manage and cleanup
sections.explanation: Enabling management for hand-opened sessions and interactively cleaning up handed-off ones, including a parser for selections typed at the prompt.

sections.title: Budgets and link
sections.explanation: `budget_set` and `budget_ls` manage soft and hard limits, and `link` manually pairs a terminal with a session found by a prefix.

sections.title: Statusline hook
sections.explanation: `hook_statusline` must never fail: it reads the Claude JSON from stdin and falls back to printing `agm`. `hook_install` adds the statusLine to ~/.claude/settings.json and reports whether it was already present.

src/model.rs.overview: Shared domain types for the whole crate: the Source enum, Usage and quota/context snapshots, and the ParseEvent/LineOutcome pair that parsers return. It also contains small utilities for summarizing text and parsing RFC 3339 timestamps with no date library.

sections.title: Source enum
sections.explanation: A closed set of agent kinds (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Agy), serialized in lowercase. `as_str` gives the stable name used in the database; match expressions elsewhere must handle each variant.

sections.title: Usage and UsageRecord
sections.explanation: `Usage` splits tokens into uncached input, cache read, cache write, output and reasoning. `total` omits reasoning because reasoning is already counted inside output. `UsageRecord` adds a dedupe_key so re-reading a log never double counts.

sections.title: Quota, context and session types
sections.explanation: QuotaWindow and QuotaSnapshot describe subscription limits per time window. ContextSnapshot holds tokens used and an optional window size, SessionMeta identifies a session, and TurnSummary with Role records short conversation turns with a byte offset back into the log.

sections.title: ParseEvent and LineOutcome
sections.explanation: A parser turns one log line into Events(Vec<ParseEvent>), Ignored, or Unknown(kind). Distinguishing Ignored from Unknown lets the ingest layer count unrecognized formats without treating known noise as errors.

sections.title: summarize
sections.explanation: Collapses whitespace and truncates to 200 characters by chars, not bytes, adding an ellipsis, so multi-byte text is never cut mid-character.

sections.title: parse_rfc3339_ms
sections.explanation: A hand-written parser for UTC timestamps with 20 or 24 characters. It validates the separators and digits, checks month lengths including leap years, then computes days since the Unix epoch with a leap-year formula. Returning None for anything unexpected keeps parsers tolerant.

src/config.rs.overview: Loads and queries configuration: providers (subscription versus API billing), per-model context windows and prices, aliases and the Policy thresholds. Built-in defaults are embedded from assets/ so agm works with no providers.toml, and the file layers user overrides on top.

sections.title: Billing and price types
sections.explanation: Billing is a two-variant enum. Price holds USD per 1M tokens for input, cache read, cache write and output, with a FREE constant for free models.

sections.title: Embedded price table
sections.explanation: `builtin_prices` parses assets/prices.toml via include_str! once through OnceLock. The `expect` is acceptable because the data ships with the binary and is covered by tests.

sections.title: Model id matching
sections.explanation: `model_id_candidates` builds ordered lookup ids: as logged, without the OpenCode provider prefix, without an 8-digit date suffix, and without an agy effort suffix. It avoids duplicates, so `claude-opus-5-5-high` still finds the base price.

sections.title: Config and Policy structs
sections.explanation: Config uses deny_unknown_fields so typos in providers.toml fail loudly. Policy has defaults for worker limits, context warning (50) and rotate (70) percentages, handoff timeouts and quota poll intervals, with serde default functions for a few fields.

sections.title: Config loading and lookups
sections.explanation: `load` returns the builtin config when the file is missing but reports other IO and parse errors with context. `model` resolves aliases and falls back to the id without its provider prefix. `context_window`, `price_for` and `billing_for_model` apply a clear precedence (user file, then built-in, then catalog) and return None instead of guessing.

sections.title: Helpers and cost
sections.explanation: `split_provider` splits at the first slash, `cost_usd` multiplies then divides by 1,000,000 once to keep precision, and `context_pct` returns None for a missing or zero window, rounded to one decimal place.

assets/prices.toml.overview: Embedded table of list API prices in USD per 1M tokens, keyed by bare model id. It is compiled into the binary by config.rs and used for `agm cost` and the TUI.

sections.title: Header and rules
sections.explanation: Comments explain the snapshot date, that only the base pricing tier is used, that missing cache_write equals input, and how dated ids, provider prefixes and effort suffixes are normalized before lookup. Users can override entries in providers.toml.

sections.title: Anthropic prices
sections.explanation: Entries for Claude Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku families with input, output, cache_read and cache_write fields, matching the Price struct.

sections.title: OpenAI and Google prices
sections.explanation: GPT and Gemini models in the same shape.

sections.title: DeepSeek and Moonshot prices
sections.explanation: Models also served by OpenCode Go, which itself is a subscription, so these prices show what usage would cost at API rates.

assets/providers.default.toml.overview: Built-in providers and model config used when the user has no providers.toml. It marks which providers bill by subscription or API and gives a few models their context windows.

sections.title: Providers and billing
sections.explanation: Codex, Claude and agy are subscriptions while openrouter and ollama are API. The `opencode-go` provider is a monthly plan. NVIDIA providers are deliberately left undeclared so costs show as unknown rather than guessed. Comments are in Vietnamese.

sections.title: Model entries
sections.explanation: gpt-6.1-sol gets a 475000 context window because OpenCode needs it, while claude-opus-5-5 leaves it empty pending confirmation. This follows the rule that nothing is guessed.

src/parse/mod.rs.overview: Defines the LogParser trait, the ParseError type and the parser_for factory that selects a parser per Source. Each agent's log format has its own submodule.

sections.title: Submodules and imports
sections.explanation: Declares the agy, claude and codex parsers and imports LineOutcome and Source from the model.

sections.title: ParseError
sections.explanation: A thiserror enum for bad JSON and for missing timestamps.

sections.title: LogParser trait
sections.explanation: `parse_line` takes one line plus its byte offset and returns a LineOutcome. `seed_model` and the optional `seed_last_ts` let the ingest layer restore parser state when resuming a file partway using a cursor.

sections.title: parser_for factory
sections.explanation: Returns a `Box<dyn LogParser>`, giving callers runtime polymorphism. OpenCode is `unreachable!` because it is read from SQLite instead of log lines.

src/parse/claude.rs.overview: Parser for Claude Code JSONL transcripts. It turns each line into session metadata, model and effort changes, token usage, context snapshots and turn summaries, matching the model events from the previous tour step.

sections.title: ClaudeParser state
sections.explanation: Keeps the current model, effort and whether session metadata has been emitted, so events are produced only when something changes. `seed_model` lets ingestion restore the model when resuming mid-file.

sections.title: Line parsing and metadata
sections.explanation: Parses the JSON line (BadJson on failure), reads type and timestamp, and emits SessionMeta once when sessionId and cwd are present. let-chains keep the conditions flat.

sections.title: Assistant lines
sections.explanation: Skips `<synthetic>` messages, emits Model and Effort only on change, and builds Usage from input, cache-read, cache-creation, output and thinking tokens. The message id becomes the dedupe_key, and used context tokens are input plus cache read plus cache write, with a saturating add. A turn summary falls back to the tool_use name when there is no text.

sections.title: User and ignored line types
sections.explanation: User text becomes a Turn. A list of known bookkeeping types is deliberately ignored, while an unknown type that produced no events returns Unknown so new formats get noticed. The final expression returns Ignored or Events.

sections.title: text_content helper
sections.explanation: Extracts text from either a plain string content or the first text block of an array.

src/parse/codex.rs.overview: Log parser for Codex rollout JSONL files. It implements the LogParser trait and turns each line (session_meta, turn_context, token_usage_record, event_msg, response_item) into model events such as usage, context, quota, and turn summaries. It is the Codex implementation in the tour's Log Parsers step.

sections.title: Parser state and seeding
sections.explanation: `CodexParser` only remembers the current model, because token_usage_record lines do not carry it. `seed_model` lets ingestion restore the model when it resumes mid-file from a saved cursor.

sections.title: Line decoding and metadata
sections.explanation: `parse_line` parses the JSON, reads `type`, `payload` and the RFC3339 timestamp (defaulting to 0 when missing). Invalid JSON becomes `ParseError::BadJson`. `session_meta` becomes a `SessionMeta` event with id, cwd, CLI version and start time.

sections.title: Model and effort turn context
sections.explanation: A `turn_context` line updates the remembered model and emits Model plus optional Effort events. Effort is read from two possible locations because `/model` can change it mid-session; lines without a model are Ignored.

sections.title: Token usage records
sections.explanation: Builds a `UsageRecord` keyed by `response_id` for dedupe. Codex's `input_tokens` includes cached tokens, so uncached input is computed with `saturating_sub(cache_read)` to avoid underflow.

sections.title: Token count: context and quota
sections.explanation: `event_msg` of type token_count yields a ContextSnapshot from the last turn's input tokens and window size, and a QuotaSnapshot from the `primary` and `secondary` rate-limit windows. `filter_map` with `?` silently drops windows with missing fields; no events means Ignored.

sections.title: Response items to turns
sections.explanation: Messages by user/assistant and tool calls become `TurnSummary` events with a short summarized text and the byte offset. Known noise item types (reasoning, outputs, compaction) are Ignored, while unrecognised ones return `Unknown` so ingestion can count them.

sections.title: Ignored and unknown kinds
sections.explanation: Top-level kinds that carry no token information are ignored, anything else is reported as Unknown. Single events are wrapped in `LineOutcome::Events` at the end.

src/parse/agy.rs.overview: Parser for Antigravity CLI `transcript.jsonl` files. Each line is a conversation step; PLANNER_RESPONSE steps carry token counts and tool calls, USER_INPUT steps carry the user request. It tracks the last timestamp because some lines lack `created_at`.

sections.title: Parser state
sections.explanation: Module docs note that `input_tokens` is uncached and `output_tokens` already includes thinking. State holds the model and `last_ts`; `seed_last_ts` keeps the maximum so a resumed parse can fill missing timestamps.

sections.title: Line header and timestamps
sections.explanation: Decodes the JSON and records `created_at` into `last_ts` when present, so later lines can fall back to it.

sections.title: User input turns
sections.explanation: USER_INPUT falls back to `last_ts` or errors with `MissingTimestamp`. The text is unwrapped from `<USER_REQUEST>` tags and summarized into a user Turn.

sections.title: Planner response usage
sections.explanation: Emits Model change events, then a Usage record when any token field exists. `output` is `max(output, thinking)` to preserve the invariant reasoning is a subset of output, and the dedupe key is `step:<index>` or the byte offset. A Context snapshot (uncached plus cache read) and an assistant Turn follow.

sections.title: Ignored step types
sections.explanation: Housekeeping step types are accepted silently; unknown types return `Unknown`. An empty event list becomes `Ignored`.

sections.title: Helper functions
sections.explanation: `extract_user_request` returns the text inside the USER_REQUEST tags or the raw text. `planner_summary` prefers content, otherwise summarizes tool call names as `[tool] a, b`.

src/ingest.rs.overview: Incremental log ingestion. It discovers JSONL files under the Codex and Claude roots, resumes each file from a saved cursor, runs the matching parser and writes events into the Store inside one transaction per file. Cursor validation by head hash detects replaced files. This is the core of the Ingestion Pipeline tour step.

sections.title: Log roots
sections.explanation: `Roots` holds the Codex sessions and Claude projects directories derived from the home directory.

sections.title: File discovery
sections.explanation: `discover_source` walks a root with walkdir, keeps `.jsonl` files (Codex only `rollout-*`) modified since `since_ms`, and counts non-NotFound walk errors. `discover` merges both sources and sorts by path for determinism.

sections.title: Batch ingestion
sections.explanation: `ingest_source` ingests each file, but a failure on one file (locked or deleted) only increments `skipped` and is logged, never aborting the scan. `ingest_all` sums both sources.

sections.title: Stats type
sections.explanation: `IngestStats` counts files, lines, events, unknown, bad and skipped lines, with an `add` accumulator.

sections.title: Hash and path key
sections.explanation: `head_hash` is FNV-1a, chosen because it is stable across Rust versions unlike DefaultHasher. `path_key` normalizes Windows paths (lowercase, backslashes) so one file never becomes two sessions and double counts tokens.

sections.title: Cursor resume logic
sections.explanation: `ingest_file` opens the file in a transaction, loads the saved cursor and hashes the first 4096 bytes. The old offset is reused only if the file did not shrink and the prefix hash matches; otherwise offset is 0 and `reset_session` clears derived data so a replaced file is not double counted.

sections.title: Parser seeding
sections.explanation: When resuming mid-file the parser is seeded with the session's stored model and last timestamp, since that context lives earlier in the file.

sections.title: Read loop and commit
sections.explanation: Reads line by line and stops at a line without trailing newline so partial writes are retried later. Each parse outcome dispatches ParseEvents to Store methods and updates stats; the cursor is saved and the transaction committed at the end.

src/opencode.rs.overview: Reads OpenCode v2 sessions from its SQLite database in read-only mode, touching only `session_v2` and `session_message` and never credential tables. It converts assistant and user messages into usage, context, model, effort and turns in the agm store. It complements the file-based ingest for the Ingestion Pipeline step.

sections.title: Imports and DB location
sections.explanation: Module docs state the read-only, two-table guarantee. `default_db` honors the `AGM_OPENCODE_DB` override and otherwise uses the standard share directory.

sections.title: Model key and message row
sections.explanation: `model_key` prefixes the model id with its providerID so the same model billed via different providers is not merged; a settings flag records that this format is in use. `Msg` mirrors the selected columns.

sections.title: Cursor and query
sections.explanation: Opens the source DB read-only with a busy timeout. The cursor is a pair (time_updated, rowid) stored in a Cursor's offset and size, so messages inserted within the same millisecond are not missed. A changed model key format forces one full rescan, safe because usage upserts by message id.

sections.title: Per-message loop setup
sections.explanation: Within a transaction on the agm store, each message maps to a session keyed `opencode://<session>`, session metadata is refreshed, and invalid JSON only counts as a bad line.

sections.title: Assistant messages
sections.explanation: Sets model and effort (ignoring the `default` variant), sums tokens, and skips streaming messages whose counters are still zero. Usage is upserted using the message id as dedupe key, and context is the sum of input and cache tokens; an assistant summary turn is inserted.

sections.title: User messages and cursor save
sections.explanation: User text becomes a summarized user turn. After the loop the max (updated, rowid) cursor is saved, the model-key flag is set after a rescan, and the transaction commits.

sections.title: Helpers
sections.explanation: `session_meta` reads directory, version and creation time from `session_v2`. `assistant_summary` picks the first non-empty text part, falling back to a `[tool] name` label; thinking-only turns give None.

src/agy.rs.overview: Scans Antigravity CLI (`agy`) sessions under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`: transcript files for tokens and a read-only summaries database for each conversation's working directory. It avoids double counting against sessions recorded by `agm ask`. Part of the Ingestion Pipeline tour step.

sections.title: Default directory
sections.explanation: Module docs describe the two data sources. `default_dir` allows the `AGM_AGY_DIR` override.

sections.title: Transcript discovery
sections.explanation: `discover` iterates `brain/<conversation_id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl`, keeping files modified since `since_ms` and returning (conversation id, path) pairs sorted by path.

sections.title: ingest_agy orchestration
sections.explanation: Loads cwds, back-fills `cwd` for already ingested file sessions (summaries can be written after the transcript's last line) but not for `agy://` ask sessions. Conversations that match the ask working directory or already have an ask session with usage are skipped. Otherwise `ingest_file` is reused, identity set, and any older duplicate ask session is deduped.

sections.title: Ask-session check
sections.explanation: `has_ask_session` returns true only if an `agy://` session for the conversation has usage rows, so transcripts remain the sole source when ask lacks usage.

sections.title: Loading workspace cwds
sections.explanation: `load_cwds` wraps `try_load_cwds`, which opens `conversation_summaries.db` read-only and maps conversation id to the first workspace path. Errors degrade to a warning and an empty map.

sections.title: URI to path conversion
sections.explanation: `first_workspace_path` parses the JSON array of URIs. `file_uri_to_path` handles localhost, UNC paths, Windows drive letters and platform separators; `percent_decode` and `hex` are a small hand-written decoder for %XX escapes.

src/hook.rs.overview: Implements `agm hook`: installing a Claude Code statusLine entry and handling the JSON Claude passes on stdin. The statusline call records plan quota (5h/7d), context window usage and terminal-to-session links, then returns a short status string. Part of the Ingestion Pipeline tour step.

sections.title: Outcome type
sections.explanation: Module docs explain why the hook exists. `InstallOutcome` distinguishes a fresh install from an already-installed hook.

sections.title: Safe installer
sections.explanation: `install_statusline` reads settings.json; only a missing file starts from empty, other errors abort rather than overwrite. An existing statusLine that already calls `hook statusline` is a no-op, anyone else's statusLine is never overwritten (an error). Otherwise it writes a command entry.

sections.title: Quota windows
sections.explanation: `statusline` extracts five_hour (300 min) and seven_day (10080 min) rate limits from the input and stores a Claude QuotaSnapshot when at least one window is present.

sections.title: Context and terminal link
sections.explanation: Finds the session via the transcript path, converts the used percentage and window size into a ContextSnapshot, and, if a herdr terminal address is provided, upserts and links the terminal to the session with source `hook`.

sections.title: Status line text
sections.explanation: Builds a one-line string: model name, context percent used, and remaining quota per window (shown as left, while context shows used).

src/store/mod.rs.overview: Core of the SQLite persistence layer. `Store` wraps a rusqlite Connection, handles WAL setup, versioned migrations (user_version up to 4) and the write API for sessions, usage, quota, turns and cursors. The v2 module adds terminals, inbox and budgets on the same type. This is the center of the SQLite Store tour step.

sections.title: Types and constants
sections.explanation: Declares the `v2` submodule and re-exports its row types. `SCHEMA_VERSION` is 4, `Cursor` stores per-file ingest progress, and `SessionStats` counts unknown and bad lines.

sections.title: Busy retry helper
sections.explanation: `retry_busy` retries SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED with exponential backoff capped at 200 ms for about 5 seconds, since some statements ignore busy_timeout.

sections.title: Opening the database
sections.explanation: Creates parent directories, opens the file or an in-memory DB, then delegates to `initialize`. In-memory is used by tests.

sections.title: Migrations
sections.explanation: If user_version is already current it returns without taking a write lock, so read-only commands do not wait for the daemon. Otherwise `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and re-read the version: <2 runs schema.sql and schema_v2.sql (with a Windows path-key rewrite from v1), <3 adds columns and the v3 index, <4 adds `sessions.effort`. Failure rolls back.

sections.title: Column helper and session identity
sections.explanation: `add_column_if_missing` checks `pragma_table_info` for idempotent ALTERs. Session helpers upsert by path, set metadata, and `dedupe_agy_ask_session` merges duplicate agy sessions in a savepoint.

sections.title: Usage, quota, context, turns
sections.explanation: Writers for model, effort, usage (upsert on session+dedupe_key, so re-parsing is idempotent), quota (ignore duplicates), context (only newer timestamps win) and turns (summary truncated to 200 chars).

sections.title: Savepoints and reset
sections.explanation: `with_savepoint` wraps writes in a named savepoint with rollback on error. `reset_session`, `refresh_last_ms`, `session_last_ts` and `add_line_stats` maintain derived per-session aggregates.

sections.title: Cursor persistence
sections.explanation: `cursor` and `save_cursor` read and upsert file progress; the 64-bit hash is cast to i64 reversibly because SQLite integers are signed. `conn` exposes the raw connection.

src/store/v2.rs.overview: Adds the v2 data access API to `Store`: herdr terminals, inter-agent messages, the user inbox, budgets, action log and settings. It defines the row structs and the SQL column mapping helpers. It builds on the schema in schema_v2.sql.

sections.title: Terminal row
sections.explanation: `TerminalRow` mirrors the terminals table, with `labels` as a BTreeMap serialized to JSON and booleans stored as integers. A manual Default provides a `handoff_state` of active.

sections.title: Other row types
sections.explanation: `InboxRow`, `MessageRow` and `BudgetRow` model the rest; a budget scope is either `task:<ID>` (tokens) or `provider:<name>:<minutes>` (percent).

sections.title: Column mapping helpers
sections.explanation: `TERM_COLS` and `term_from` keep the SELECT column order and row decoding in one place; labels JSON decodes leniently.

sections.title: Terminal upsert and updates
sections.explanation: `upsert_terminal` uses COALESCE so existing values survive partial updates and promotes `agm.task`/`agm.role` labels. Other methods set labels, status, turn, app and finish or remove terminals.

sections.title: Linking and covered-since
sections.explanation: Context window size, terminal-session links, launch spec and handoff state setters. `covered_since` tracks, per source, the earliest time already scanned using settings keys and keeps the minimum.

sections.title: Terminal queries
sections.explanation: `terminal` resolves by address or name, preferring exact address and live state; `terminals` can filter to live ones.

sections.title: Inbox
sections.explanation: `open_inbox` inserts only if no identical open item exists, in one atomic statement. `open_inbox_keyed` dedupes by terminal, source and kind and refreshes the text instead (for example 86% to 87% context). Resolve methods close items, including in bulk via a savepoint.

sections.title: Messages, actions, settings, budgets
sections.explanation: Message add, status and list, `log_action`, a key-value settings store with upsert, and budget set, list and remove (returns whether a row was deleted).

src/store/schema.sql.overview: Version 1 SQLite schema: sessions, per-response usage, quota snapshots, conversation turns and file cursors. All creates are idempotent so migration code can run it safely.

sections.title: Sessions table
sections.explanation: One row per log source file or session, with a UNIQUE `path`, optional id, cwd, version, timing, model, latest context snapshot and unknown/bad line counters.

sections.title: Usage and quota
sections.explanation: `usage` stores token buckets per response with UNIQUE(session, dedupe_key), enabling idempotent upserts. `quota` holds provider window snapshots unique per provider, timestamp and window length.

sections.title: Turns and cursors
sections.explanation: `turns` are conversation summaries unique per byte offset. `cursors` track offset, size, mtime and head hash per file for incremental reads.

src/store/schema_v2.sql.overview: Version 2 schema adding the orchestration tables used by the daemon and herdr integration: terminals, messages, inbox, budgets, actions, rotations and settings.

sections.title: Terminals
sections.explanation: One row per herdr terminal keyed by address, with labels JSON, task and role, lifecycle state, timing, exit code and an optional link to a session.

sections.title: Messages and inbox
sections.explanation: `messages` records agent-to-agent traffic with a delivery status. `inbox` holds items needing the user, with `resolved_ms` and an optional reply.

sections.title: Budgets and actions
sections.explanation: `budgets` define soft and hard limits per scope with an action; `actions` is an audit log of interventions with an ok flag.

sections.title: Rotations and settings
sections.explanation: `rotations` track context-rotation handoffs from an old terminal to a new one, and `settings` is a simple key-value table.

src/store/schema_v3.sql.overview: Tiny version 3 migration script. Only the index lives here because new columns are added by Rust code.

sections.title: Usage timestamp index
sections.explanation: The comment explains new columns on rotations and terminals are added idempotently by `add_column_if_missing` in `Store::initialize`. The script creates an index on usage(ts_ms) for time-range statistics queries.

src/codex_quota.rs.overview: Fetches Codex plan quota by spawning `codex app-server --stdio` and calling the JSON-RPC method `account/rateLimits/read`, which costs no tokens. It parses the result into a QuotaSnapshot and provides a non-blocking poller for the daemon. Failures never write fake values. This is the Codex part of the Quota and System Metering tour step.

sections.title: Module contract and parsing
sections.explanation: Docs state the guarantees: read-only quota, used percent stored as-is, windows of 300 and 10080 minutes. `parse_usage` accepts either a full JSON-RPC response or just the result, and discards windows with missing fields, unexpected durations or percentages outside 0-100, bailing if none remain.

sections.title: Recording
sections.explanation: `record_usage` parses then inserts each snapshot into the store.

sections.title: Fetching with timeout
sections.explanation: `FETCH_TIMEOUT` is 8 seconds for the whole process. `fetch_usage` spawns the binary (overridable by `AGM_CODEX_BIN`) and kills the whole process tree on error.

sections.title: JSON-RPC exchange
sections.explanation: A reader thread forwards stdout lines over a channel. The code sends initialize (id 1), waits, then sends `account/rateLimits/read` (id 2), surfacing JSON-RPC errors and returning the result.

sections.title: Waiting and killing
sections.explanation: `wait_for_id` polls the channel in 200 ms slices against the deadline and ignores unrelated lines. `kill_tree` uses `taskkill /T /F` on Windows because wrapper shims can keep stdout open.

sections.title: Background poller
sections.explanation: `CodexQuotaPoller` runs `fetch` on a thread, collects it on later `tick` calls without blocking the daemon loop, and starts a new fetch only when the interval has elapsed. `warn` prints each distinct error once.

src/agy_quota.rs.overview: Reads Antigravity (`agy`) subscription quota by running `agy --print /usage` and turning its JSON into `QuotaSnapshot` rows. It also provides a background poller so the daemon never blocks on the roughly three-second CLI call. This is the Antigravity half of tour step 7's quota metering.

sections.title: Module docs and imports
sections.explanation: The doc comment records key facts: the call costs no tokens, agy reports the remaining fraction while agm stores the used percent, and three independent quota groups become three providers. Provider names avoid `:` because budget scopes are split on that character.

sections.title: Provider and window mapping
sections.explanation: `PROVIDERS` maps bucket id prefixes to provider names, with the longer `gemini-argon-` listed before `gemini-` so the first `starts_with` match is the right one. `UsageParse` counts `unknown` buckets and deliberately skipped `disabled` ones. `window_minutes` only knows `5h` and `weekly`.

sections.title: parse_usage
sections.explanation: Parses the stdout JSON and fails on a non-SUCCESS status or a missing `groups` array rather than guessing. Each bucket needs a known provider, window, a finite remaining fraction in 0..=1 and a parsable reset time; otherwise it is counted as unknown. Used percent is `(1 - remaining) * 100`, clamped, and windows are grouped per provider in a `BTreeMap` for stable output.

sections.title: record_usage and fetch_usage
sections.explanation: `record_usage` parses and then inserts each snapshot into the shared `quota` table, so Codex, Claude and agy all use the same storage. `fetch_usage` runs the binary (overridable via `AGM_AGY_BIN`) in a temp work dir outside the repo and errors with a stderr excerpt if nothing is printed.

sections.title: AgyQuotaPoller
sections.explanation: The poller keeps an mpsc receiver for an in-flight fetch. Each `tick` first collects a finished result (non-blocking `try_recv`), then starts a new thread when the interval has elapsed. `interval_min = 0` disables it, and `warn` deduplicates repeated identical errors so the daemon log is not spammed. The `Fetch` closure type makes it injectable in tests.

src/opencode_quota.rs.overview: Fetches OpenCode Go plan limits via `opencode api GET /api/experimental/usage/limits` and stores them as the `opencode-go` provider. Like its agy sibling it parses defensively and polls on a worker thread. It is part of tour step 7's quota metering.

sections.title: Parsing the limits JSON
sections.explanation: `parse_usage` reads `data.go` and maps the `rolling`, `weekly` and `monthly` meters to 300, 10080 and 43200 minute windows. Null data or a missing `go` object is not an error and yields no snapshots, and bad or unknown meters increment `unknown` instead of being recorded as 0% or 100%. The API's `percent` is already used percent, so it is only clamped. The per-window `limited` flag is returned separately.

sections.title: Recording to store
sections.explanation: `record_usage` inserts snapshots into the quota table and, since that table has no `limited` column, saves the flag as settings keys `quota_limited:opencode-go:<minutes>`.

sections.title: Fetching with a deadline
sections.explanation: `fetch_usage` uses a 5 second overall deadline and on Windows tries both `opencode` and `opencode.cmd` unless `AGM_OPENCODE_BIN` is set. `fetch_with` spawns the child and reads stdout on a helper thread so the timeout can be enforced from the main thread.

sections.title: kill_tree
sections.explanation: On timeout the whole process tree is killed (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows) because a `.cmd` shim can leave a grandchild holding the stdout pipe open, which would hang the reader thread.

sections.title: OpenCodeQuotaPoller
sections.explanation: Same design as the agy poller: a thread per poll, results collected non-blockingly on the next `tick`, interval 0 disables it, and errors are logged once per distinct message.

src/sysmon.rs.overview: Live RAM, CPU, disk and per-agent process load readings that power `agm sys` and the TUI header. Nothing is stored in the database. Sampling the OS is isolated in `SysSampler`, while classification and attribution are pure functions that tests can call directly. It is the system-metering half of tour step 7.

sections.title: Data types
sections.explanation: Imports `sysinfo` and defines serializable stat structs: `MemStats`, `CpuStats`, `DiskStats` (with `volume_id` and `also_mounted_at` for de-duplication), `AgentLoad` and the aggregate `SysStats`. CPU and rates are `Option` so a missing reading is never shown as a fake 0.

sections.title: Formatting helpers
sections.explanation: `fullest_disk` picks the fullest non-removable disk for the one-line summary, `mount_label` shortens `C:\` to `C:`, `pct` returns `None` for a zero total, and `human_bytes` uses binary units like Task Manager.

sections.title: Agent classification
sections.explanation: `agent_of` labels a process as an agent by executable name, adds an `-app` suffix for Store or macOS bundle desktop apps, and recognises npm installs running under `node` or `bun` by scanning the command line for package names.

sections.title: Process attribution
sections.explanation: `attribute` walks each process up its parent chain (max 64 hops) to the nearest agent ancestor and sums count, memory and CPU per agent. A parent that started after its child is treated as a reused pid and ignored. CPU is divided by logical cores to give a machine share, and results are sorted by memory.

sections.title: Disk merging and volume ids
sections.explanation: `merge_disks` folds duplicate mounts and mounts sharing a real volume id into one entry. `volume_id` has three `cfg` variants: Windows volume GUID, Unix device id, and a fallback returning `None`. `skip_fs` drops pseudo file systems.

sections.title: SysSampler
sections.explanation: Holds the `sysinfo` handles because CPU percent and I/O rates are deltas between readings. `new` takes two baseline process refreshes spaced by `MINIMUM_CPU_UPDATE_INTERVAL` to work around Windows lacking a first-refresh baseline. `sample` returns the cached reading if called too soon, otherwise refreshes everything and builds `SysStats`.

sections.title: read_once
sections.explanation: One-shot helper for CLI use that sleeps long enough for the CPU and disk rates to be meaningful before sampling.

src/hc.rs.overview: The wrapper around the herdr-core `hc` CLI. Everything goes through the `Hc` trait so tests can use fakes, and `HcCli` is the real implementation that shells out with `--json`. It also holds template loading and the conversion from hc terminal objects to store rows. This is the herdr integration of tour step 8.

sections.title: Errors and template loading
sections.explanation: `HcFailure` carries hc's structured `{kind, message}` error, and `is_missing_sh` detects the Windows case where hc cannot find `sh`. `load_template` is a read-only fallback that validates the name, locates the template dir (`AGM_HC_TEMPLATES`, `%APPDATA%` or `~/.config`), parses the front matter and accepts only a single plain `command:` with no shell metacharacters.

sections.title: Hc trait and RunSpec
sections.explanation: `RunSpec` is the argv, name, cwd and labels for a new terminal. The `Hc` trait lists ls, get, send, run, kill, interrupt and templates. `send` has `if_idle` and `force` flags: the first types only when the target is idle and the second answers a blocked prompt. `HcCli` takes its binary from `AGM_HC_BIN`.

sections.title: Calling the CLI
sections.explanation: `call` runs the binary and parses stdout as JSON, falling back to a string. hc may report errors as an `error` object on stdout or stderr even with a zero exit code, so that is checked first and turned into `HcFailure`; otherwise a non-zero exit becomes a generic error.

sections.title: Argument builders
sections.explanation: `run_args` and `send_args` are pure functions that build the argument vectors. Flags precede a `--` separator so that user text beginning with `-` is never read as a flag, and `run` always passes `--bg --outlive-parent`.

sections.title: Hc implementation for HcCli
sections.explanation: Each trait method maps to one `hc <cmd> --json` call and extracts the relevant field (`terminals`, `templates`), returning `()` for kill and interrupt.

sections.title: Terminal object to row
sections.explanation: `app_from_argv` guesses the app from argv when the program has not reported itself (stripping shim extensions, and mapping `claude` to `claude-code` and `agy` to `antigravity`). `effective_cwd` prefers the foreground process directory. `terminal_row_from` normalizes the different shapes hc uses for snapshots, events, `ls` and `get` into one `TerminalRow`, reading task and role from the `agm.*` labels.

src/daemon.rs.overview: Applies lines from the `hc events --json` stream to the store: terminals are created, updated, finished and removed, and inbox items open and close as agents become blocked. It contains only event handling and no loop. It is the event-ingest part of tour step 8.

sections.title: apply_event dispatch
sections.explanation: Handles three line shapes: an initial or post-`missed` snapshot, a `missed` marker carrying a snapshot, and normal `event` messages dispatched on `type`. Unknown types are ignored so new events from herdr do not break the daemon. `finished`, `lost` and `removed` also resolve the terminal's open `blocked` inbox items, and a `foreground` event only guesses the app while the terminal has not self-reported.

sections.title: apply_snapshot
sections.explanation: A snapshot is the complete set of live terminals. Any terminal still marked live in the DB but absent from the snapshot died while the daemon was down, so it is finished and its inbox is resolved, freeing worker slots and avoiding bogus policy actions.

sections.title: apply_terminal and apply_status
sections.explanation: `apply_terminal` upserts via `terminal_row_from` and applies any embedded status. `apply_status` accepts both the object form and the plain string form, records status, kind, message and turn, and opens a `blocked` inbox item with a generated text when needed. Any other state resolves the blocked item.

src/correlate.rs.overview: Links herdr terminals to ingested log sessions so usage can be attributed to the right agent terminal. It links only on a two-way unique match and never overwrites hook or manual links. Part of tour step 8.

sections.title: Constants and normalization
sections.explanation: Documents the trust order and the time window: a session counts as a candidate if it started from 1 minute before to 10 minutes after the terminal was created. `norm_cwd` normalizes separators, strips the verbatim path prefix and lower-cases on Windows. `source_for_app` maps hc app names to log sources.

sections.title: link_all candidate search
sections.explanation: For each live terminal that has app and cwd, and is not tagged `agm.parent_rotation`, it queries unlinked sessions of the right source within the time window and filters them by normalized cwd. OpenCode is special: one TUI hosts many sessions, so the window is open-ended, an auto link may advance to a newer session, and only the newest candidate is kept.

sections.title: Uniqueness check and linking
sections.explanation: It counts how many terminals claim each session and links only when a terminal has exactly one candidate and that session has exactly one claimant. Ambiguous cases stay unlinked rather than risk mis-attributing usage.

sections.title: link_codex_rotation
sections.explanation: Deterministically links a Codex successor by looking for the `[agm-rot:<id>]` tag at the start of a user turn after the rotation request, with the same normalized cwd and no existing terminal. It runs in a transaction and the UPDATE re-checks that nothing else claimed the session, setting `link_source = 'rotation'`.

src/actions.rs.overview: The audited intervention layer: send and reply to messages, spawn agents with limits, kill or interrupt with protection rules, bulk inbox dismissal and post-rotation cleanup. Its central rule is that Codex and Claude sessions are only stopped by a confirmed human, while agents may stop only OpenCode workers. Tour step 9.

sections.title: Message kinds
sections.explanation: Message types are stored as Vietnamese codes (such as `GIAO` and `BÁO CÁO`) and mapped to English display names (`ASSIGN`, `REPORT`) by `kind_to_english` and `kind_from_english`, keeping stored data stable while the UI is English.

sections.title: Caller classification
sections.explanation: `Caller` is either a confirmed or unconfirmed user or an agent. `classify_caller` treats a TTY not owned by an agent as a user. `detect_caller` fails closed: if the calling terminal cannot be inspected, or runs a known agent app or has self-reported, the caller is an agent. `PROTECTED_APPS` and `AGENT_KILLABLE_APPS` hold the policy lists.

sections.title: Done selectors and filters
sections.explanation: Parses `agm done` selectors such as `N`, `N-M` and `N,M-K` into ids, tracks the legacy single-id form, and defines filters and report types. `normalize_done_kind` and `normalize_done_source` accept English aliases and validate sources.

sections.title: dismiss_done and dismiss
sections.explanation: Bulk-dismisses inbox items by ids or filters and returns what was done and skipped. `blocked` items are skipped unless `--source blocked` was explicit, and the legacy single-id path stays strict about missing items. `dismiss` closes one item without typing into any terminal.

sections.title: send and reply
sections.explanation: `format_message` builds the standard message line. `send` validates the kind, always records the message, and either opens an inbox item for `user` or calls `hc send`. It drops the `--if idle` guard only when the target is in `done`, because hc rejects that guard for finished agents. `reply` types into the originating terminal, forcing the input for `blocked` items, and logs the action.

sections.title: Spawn precheck
sections.explanation: `SpawnReq` describes a spawn. `spawn_precheck` validates the task id and template, enforces `max_workers` for the `worker` role (excluding the terminal being replaced), checks the hard task budget and generates a `w-<task>-<n>` name. `spawn_successor_precheck` is the equivalent for Claude and Codex successors.

sections.title: spawn and rotation prepare
sections.explanation: `spawn` decides if the name is an hc template, builds a `RunSpec` with `agm.task` and `agm.role` labels, and on Windows falls back to running the template's command directly when `sh` is missing, then sends the brief by hand. It logs the action and upserts the new terminal. `prepare_rotation_spawn` verifies how a successor can receive its brief before anything is killed and fails closed.

sections.title: Brief delivery failure
sections.explanation: `EXIT_BRIEF_UNDELIVERED` (3) and the `BriefUndelivered` error represent a terminal that opened but never received its brief, so scripts do not clean up the worktree or spawn a duplicate. `exit_code` maps errors to exit codes and `send_spawn_brief` performs the delivery.

sections.title: authorize, manage, kill, interrupt
sections.explanation: `authorize` is the guard: unconfirmed users are refused, confirmed users pass, agents may only act on OpenCode and are refused on protected apps. Refusals are logged and agents' refusals open a `request` inbox item for the human. `set_managed_launch` only lets a confirmed user turn on management and store the `LaunchSpec`. `kill` and `interrupt` authorize, call hc and log.

sections.title: Cleanup of handed-off sessions
sections.explanation: `eligible_cleanups` selects rotations in `done` whose old terminal is `handed_off` and either finished or replaced by a live linked successor. `fresh_cleanup_terminal` re-verifies the terminal's identity via `hc get`. `execute_cleanup_batch` accepts only a confirmed user and re-checks every item right before removing, while preserving sessions, usage, rotations and handoff files.

src/policy.rs.overview: Policy checks run on each daemon tick: budget thresholds for tasks and providers, and context-fill warnings. All automatic actions can be switched off with `agm policy off`. Tour step 9.

sections.title: Enable switch and task tokens
sections.explanation: `enabled` reads the `policy` setting and is on unless it equals `off`. `task_tokens` sums input, cache and output tokens over all sessions linked to terminals of the task.

sections.title: Provider percent
sections.explanation: `provider_percent` takes the latest quota row, returns `None` if it is stale, and otherwise computes an effective used percent. A window that has already reset counts as 0 so an old 96% does not keep triggering thresholds.

sections.title: Budget values and spawn gate
sections.explanation: A budget scope is `task:<id>` (tokens) or `provider:<name>:<window>` (percent). `spawn_blocked_by_budget` refuses new spawns when a task's hard limit is already exceeded.

sections.title: Context percent and notify
sections.explanation: `session_context_pct` reads context use from the session row and uses the model's configured window when the log has none. `notify` opens a `budget` inbox item and, if a manager terminal is configured, messages it through `actions::send`, ignoring send errors.

sections.title: Budget and context ticks
sections.explanation: `budgets_tick` remembers the highest level reached per budget in a setting, so it only acts when the level rises and resets when the value drops below soft. On a hard breach it can kill or interrupt the task's terminals, but only via `actions` as the `agm-policy` agent, so protected apps are refused. `context_tick` opens a warning for sessions above `ctx_warn`. `tick` runs both.

src/rotation.rs.overview: The state machine that rotates a session when its context fills up. OpenCode workers are handed off, killed and respawned, while managed Claude Code and Codex sessions get a handoff file and a successor with no kill of the old session. State is persisted in the `rotations` table. Tour step 9.

sections.title: Types and constants
sections.explanation: Documents the two flows and the states: `pending`, `requested`, `handoff_ready`, `spawning`, `awaiting_link`, `done`. `HANDOFF_MARKER` is the sentinel line an agent writes last, and `Rotation` mirrors a row of the table.

sections.title: Prompt texts and readiness
sections.explanation: Builders for the handoff request, resume prompt and successor prompt (Codex gets an `[agm-rot:<id>]` tag for later linking). `is_handoff_ready` checks the file is long enough, contains `rotation_id: <id>`, and ends with the marker.

sections.title: Eligibility and state helpers
sections.explanation: `rotatable_*` predicates define who may rotate, `active` loads in-flight rotations, and `set_state`, `fail` and `needs_attention` persist transitions, open inbox items and log actions. `fail` keeps the old session and suggests `agm rotate` to retry.

sections.title: start
sections.explanation: Creates a `pending` row unless one is active or the terminal is already `handed_off`. Automatic starts also skip terminals with a prior failed or needs-attention rotation to avoid repeated handoff nagging. The cwd comes from the confirmed `launch_spec` or the terminal.

sections.title: tick
sections.explanation: First detects sessions over `ctx_rotate` and starts rotations, or raises a keyed `unmanaged` inbox item for manually opened Claude or Codex sessions. Then it advances every active rotation along the OpenCode or interactive branch.

sections.title: OpenCode flow
sections.explanation: `advance_opencode` validates the terminal, requests the handoff and waits for a new turn while idle. `verify_and_respawn` checks git state (a new commit touching the log file and a clean worktree) and only then spawns the successor, waiting until timeout otherwise.

sections.title: Interactive flow
sections.explanation: `fresh_idle_status` re-reads hc to confirm the terminal is idle. `advance_interactive` is a match over states: `pending` asks for a handoff file, `requested` waits for a valid file, `handoff_ready` spawns using the stored `LaunchSpec`, `spawning` recovers a crash by finding the labeled terminal, and `awaiting_link` waits for correlation and then marks the old terminal `handed_off`. Timeouts become `needs_attention`.

src/launch.rs.overview: Parses, sanitizes and rebuilds the command line used to start a successor Claude Code or Codex session (`LaunchSpec`). It is deliberately strict: unknown flags are rejected so a rotation never replays something unsafe or ambiguous. Tour step 9.

sections.title: LaunchSpec
sections.explanation: A versioned struct holding app, executable, filtered argv and cwd, with JSON round-trip that validates the version and that the executable is not blank.

sections.title: Command tokenizer
sections.explanation: `parse_cmd_tokens` splits `--cmd` strings into args handling single and double quotes without invoking a shell, and rejects unterminated quotes or empty input. `is_shell` recognises shell executables.

sections.title: Extracting and building
sections.explanation: `extract_launch_argv` pulls the agent argv from `hc get` (foreground first), skipping shells. `parse_launch_spec` checks the app matches and applies the per-app filter. `build_successor_argv` always inserts `--` before the prompt so variadic flags such as `--add-dir` cannot swallow it.

sections.title: Claude hook check
sections.explanation: `check_claude_hook_installed` reads `~/.claude/settings.json` and requires a `hook statusline` command, because Claude rotation depends on that hook for context data.

sections.title: Codex filter
sections.explanation: `filter_codex` uses allowlists of flags with values, zero-arg flags and flags to strip (`-C` since cwd is set separately). It drops `resume` or `fork` plus their session id, discards the old trailing prompt and rejects non-interactive subcommands.

sections.title: Claude filter
sections.explanation: `filter_claude` has the same shape with extra cases: variadic flags that consume arguments until the next flag, flags stripped like `--continue` and `--resume`, and a rejection of `-p` or `--print` because rotation needs an interactive session.

src/branches.rs.overview: Reads and edits `### <repo>/<branch>` blocks of BRANCHES.md safely. The first half is pure text manipulation; the second adds a directory lock, atomic writes and a git-verified `ready` guard. Tour step 10.

sections.title: Vocabulary and validation
sections.explanation: `STATUSES` and `FIELDS` define the allowed values. `validate_entry` requires `repo/branch` names of lower-case characters, and `validate_fields` rejects unknown, duplicate, blank, multi-line or ` # `-containing values (they would read back as comments) and invalid statuses.

sections.title: Parsing the markdown
sections.explanation: `parse_field` recognises `- key: value` lines, `strip_comment` removes trailing comments, and `find_block` locates a heading (ignoring a BOM) and errors if the entry appears twice. `read_entry` returns the parsed fields.

sections.title: upsert_entry
sections.explanation: Updates fields in place, appends missing ones after the last field, or creates a new block at the end. Duplicate keys keep the last value and the original line ending style (CRLF or LF) is preserved.

sections.title: Directory lock
sections.explanation: The lock is an atomically created directory with an `owner` token file. `Drop` removes it only if the token is still ours, so a lock that was reclaimed as stale is left alone. `acquire_lock` and `acquire_lock_with` poll until timeout, with injectable create and rename for tests.

sections.title: Writer permission and types
sections.explanation: `ensure_writer` forbids terminals with the `worker` role from writing the registry. `BranchUpdate` and `UpdateOutcome` are the request and result, and `get` treats a missing file as no entry.

sections.title: Ready guard and atomic write
sections.explanation: `check_ready` demands a 12-40 hex SHA head, a worktree, a clean tree, and that the real HEAD matches the declared head. `write_atomic_with` writes a temp file and renames, retrying on Windows sharing violations.

sections.title: do_update and update
sections.explanation: `do_update` validates, requires an existing `BRANCHES.md`, runs git checks before taking the lock (git can be slower than the stale timeout) and then under the lock only compares strings, upserts and writes atomically. `update` wraps it and logs the action even on failure.

src/git.rs.overview: A minimal read-only git layer behind a `Git` trait, used to verify handoffs and branch readiness. Tour step 10.

sections.title: Git trait and runner
sections.explanation: The trait offers `head`, `is_clean` and `touched_since`, so callers can substitute fakes. The private `git` helper runs `git -C <cwd>` and turns a failing exit into an error with stderr.

sections.title: GitCli implementation
sections.explanation: `is_clean` treats untracked files as dirty but excludes the orchestration dirs `.agents/tasks` and `.agents/.runtime`. `touched_since` returns the newest commit in `since..HEAD` that touched a path, or `None`.

sections.title: ensure_handoff_excluded
sections.explanation: Appends `.agents/handoff/` to the repo's `info/exclude` found via `git rev-parse --git-path` (so it works in worktrees), idempotently and keeping newline hygiene. It returns `false` for non-repos.

src/mcp.rs.overview: A synchronous, stdio-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) server speaking JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, with no tokio. It exposes seven agm tools (send, inbox, ps, quota, spawn, branch_get, branch_update) so agents can call agm with a JSON Schema instead of typing CLI commands. The tour step on the BRANCHES.md writer and MCP server points here as the place where agents reach agm directly.

sections.title: Context and error types
sections.explanation: The module doc states the protocol rules: stdout carries only JSON-RPC, logs go to stderr. `McpCtx` bundles the `Store`, trait objects for `Hc` and `Git` (so tests can inject fakes), the config path, the caller terminal and an injectable clock. `ToolError` separates an unknown tool (a JSON-RPC error) from a tool that ran and failed (reported as `isError` content).

sections.title: Tool definitions
sections.explanation: `tool()` builds a tool descriptor with an `inputSchema` that sets `additionalProperties: false`. `tool_definitions()` lists exactly the seven Phase 1 tools; there is deliberately no kill, interrupt or cleanup tool. Message kinds are an English enum, with Vietnamese aliases accepted later in `agm_send`.

sections.title: Argument helpers and guards
sections.explanation: `opt_bool`, `opt_str` and `req_str` give typed argument access with errors naming the offending parameter. `mcp_actor` makes the sender the calling terminal or the literal "agent", never "user", so an MCP client cannot impersonate the human. `abs_branches_file` requires an absolute path because the server's cwd is untrusted, and `reject_unknown_keys` enforces the schema's no-extra-properties rule at runtime.

sections.title: call_tool: write tools
sections.explanation: Dispatches on the tool name after rejecting unknown keys. `agm_send` maps the kind via `kind_from_english` (falling back to stored codes), then calls `actions::send` and turns a `failed` row into an error just like the CLI. `agm_spawn` builds a `SpawnReq` and loads config before `actions::spawn`. `agm_branch_update` validates that `fields` is an object of strings, then delegates to `branches::update` under its lock with the caller identity so worker terminals can be refused.

sections.title: call_tool: read tools
sections.explanation: `agm_ps` and `agm_inbox` read live or open rows unless `all` is set. `agm_quota` combines `report::quota_with_config` with an optional per-task token total from `policy::task_tokens`. `agm_branch_get` only reads a file literally named BRANCHES.md, a small path-restriction safeguard; the final arm returns `Unknown`.

sections.title: JSON-RPC response wrapping
sections.explanation: `ok` and `err` build JSON-RPC envelopes. `tools_call` is the single place that wraps results: success carries both pretty text and `structuredContent` with `isError: false`, an unknown tool maps to code -32602, and a failed tool is a normal result with `isError: true` and the full anyhow chain (`{e:#}`).

sections.title: Method dispatch
sections.explanation: `handle_message` returns `None` for messages without an `id` (notifications get no reply). `initialize` echoes the client's protocol version only when it is in `PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`, else the newest. It also handles `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call`, answering other methods with -32601.

sections.title: Line-oriented serve loop
sections.explanation: `write_line` writes one JSON value per line and flushes. `serve` reads raw bytes up to each newline, so invalid UTF-8 produces a -32700 parse error instead of aborting. Blank lines are skipped, batches are rejected with -32600, and objects go to `handle_message`. The loop ends only when stdin reaches EOF, so garbage input never kills the server.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-22-agm-mc.overview: An implementation plan (written in Vietnamese) for agm Phase 1: the `agm mcp` stdio server and the `agm branch` command that edits BRANCHES.md under an atomic lock. It is organised as seven test-first tasks with explicit review focus areas, and it is the design record behind src/mcp.rs and src/branches.rs in the tour's MCP step.

sections.title: Goal, architecture and adjustments
sections.explanation: States the goal (typed MCP tools instead of error-prone PowerShell CLI calls, plus locked BRANCHES.md writes), the two new modules and the tech stack. The numbered adjustments to the spec fix the target version at 0.4.0, avoid any schema change, use English message-kind enums with Vietnamese aliases, defer workflow tools to Phase 2, share the lock directory with the legacy `mkdir` protocol, and refuse worker terminals.

sections.title: Global constraints
sections.explanation: Hard rules for every task: no new crates, no tokio, tests, clippy and fmt green after each task, mcp.rs never builds `Caller::User`, stdout carries only JSON-RPC, and lock timings (60 s stale, 30 s wait) plus the valid status and key lists are fixed.

sections.title: Review focus
sections.explanation: Lists five risks to check: CRLF preservation on Windows, orphaned locks, a missing terminal ID making the sender "agent" rather than "user", robustness to malformed JSON-RPC, and values with `#` or Vietnamese text surviving round trips. Each maps to a named test in a task.

sections.title: Tasks 1-2: branches module
sections.explanation: Task 1 builds pure functions to read and upsert `### <lane>/<slug>` blocks, with tests for inline comments, CRLF and duplicate headings. Task 2 adds directory locking, atomic tmp-then-rename writes, and a guarded `update` that checks the ready state and refuses workers. Each task follows the same write failing test, implement, rerun, commit rhythm.

sections.title: Tasks 3-4: CLI and MCP skeleton
sections.explanation: Task 3 wires `agm branch get|set` into the CLI via `ops::branch_get` and `ops::branch_set`. Task 4 creates the JSON-RPC framework with tests for version negotiation, notifications, error codes, surviving garbage input, and a source-level assertion that `Caller::User` never appears in mcp.rs.

sections.title: Tasks 5-6: tools and guards
sections.explanation: Task 5 adds the four read-only tools. Task 6 adds the write tools, with tests that the tool list is exactly the Phase 1 set, that a send without a terminal ID is from "agent", that spawn respects `max_workers`, that workers cannot update branches, and that no tool call ever kills.

sections.title: Task 7: docs and release
sections.explanation: Covers the docs update, version 0.4.0, automated verification (fmt, clippy, tests) and a real-world check by registering the server in Claude Code and confirming an `agm_send` to the user lands in the inbox with the terminal address as sender.

src/report.rs.overview: The read-side query layer: it turns the SQLite store into session lists, cost and usage summaries, quota rows and recent turns. It also owns the local-time window arithmetic (today, month, last N months) that the dashboard and CLI both rely on. It is the data source for the Reporting, TUI and Dashboard tour step.

sections.title: Row and window types
sections.explanation: Imports plus the serializable report shapes: `SessionRow`, `GroupBy`, `UsageWindow`, `UsageBucket`, `UsageSummary`, `LocalBounds`, `CostRow` and `QuotaRow`. Fields such as `stale`, `reset_passed` and `limited` carry quota freshness state to the UI.

sections.title: Quota percent helpers
sections.explanation: `effective_used_percent` treats a quota window whose reset time has passed as 0% used, because the old figure is no longer valid. `left_percent` converts to remaining percent, clamps to 0-100 and keeps NaN so the UI can show unknown. `USAGE_SUMS` is the shared SQL aggregate fragment.

sections.title: Sessions query
sections.explanation: `source_from` and `usage_at` decode rows into model types, and `sessions` joins sessions with their usage to produce `SessionRow`s since a timestamp, computing cost and context percent through config helpers.

sections.title: Calendar and local-time math
sections.explanation: Hand-written `civil_from_days` and `days_from_civil` convert between epoch days and dates without a date crate. `compute_local_bounds` derives the 24h, today, month and N-months starts, taking an `offset_at` closure so tests can fake the time zone. `sqlite_offset_at` obtains the real UTC offset from SQLite's `'localtime'` and caches it per hour; `window_since_ms` selects one bound.

sections.title: Cost aggregation
sections.explanation: `CostAcc` accumulates per-key token and cost totals, `price_row` prices a row from the config table, and `cost_totals`, `value_label` and `cost`/`cost_with_offset` group by session, model or day. Unknown-model tokens are tracked as unpriced rather than counted as zero cost.

sections.title: Usage summary and coverage
sections.explanation: `usage_summary_with_offset` scans the usage rows once from the earliest needed bound and buckets them into the 24h, today and month totals plus per-month rows. `coverage_status` checks whether history reaches back far enough so the TUI knows if a backfill is needed.

sections.title: Bars and quota rows
sections.explanation: `render_bar` and `spark_bar` draw ASCII or Unicode bars. `quota_with_config` selects the latest quota row per (provider, window) with a correlated MAX subquery and flags `limited` from settings. `quota_is_stale` marks data stale when older than `quota_stale_min` or when newer usage exists for the same plan. This feeds the agm_quota MCP tool too.

sections.title: Session resolution and turns
sections.explanation: `package_has_usage_after` supports the stale check. `resolve_session` finds a unique session by id prefix and errors on zero or ambiguous matches, listing the candidates. `turns` returns the last N turns of a session in chronological order by querying descending and reversing.

src/dashboard.rs.overview: A pure rendering module for the `agm tui` dashboard: it builds a `Snapshot` from the database and renders ANSI text with comfy-table, with no stdin or stdout I/O. It also parses the typed TUI commands. It is the operator-facing view in the Reporting, TUI and Dashboard tour step; it renders with hand-written ANSI escapes rather than a TUI library.

sections.title: Imports, palette and view types
sections.explanation: Imports comfy-table, unicode width and segmentation crates and the report, policy and store types, then defines the ANSI escape constants used through `paint`. `TermView`, `BudgetView` and `Snapshot` are the flat structures renderers read: `tokens` is `None` for an unlinked terminal (unknown, not zero) and `system` is filled by the TUI because the database has no live machine stats.

sections.title: snapshot builder
sections.explanation: For each live terminal it fetches linked-session token totals, model, effort, cwd and context percent, finds the latest message to or from it (matching address or name), and composes a status string like `BLOCKED (kind)` plus `[HANDED OFF]`. It then reads completed rotation pairs, budget values, quota, usage summary, inbox and the last 5 messages.

sections.title: Formatting helpers and cells
sections.explanation: Small helpers for painting, padding by display width, ages, colour thresholds, bars, token abbreviations, terminal tables and cell styling (status, effort, context, message kind badges), plus word-wrapping that respects ANSI sequences. Width-aware padding keeps tables aligned with CJK and emoji.

sections.title: Header, system and footer
sections.explanation: Renders the header, the machine meters (CPU cores, RAM, disk, per-agent resource lines with sparklines), the system verdict and the command footer. `bounded_block` limits line width so wide content never wraps the pane.

sections.title: Section selection
sections.explanation: The `Section` enum lists the selectable dashboard areas, with `MAX_VIEW = 3` and a default of quota, terminals and inbox. `parse_view` validates the user's `view` arguments. Recent messages are pinned separately and do not count against the limit.

sections.title: Frame assembly
sections.explanation: `render` shows all sections; `render_view` assembles header, chosen sections, recent messages and footer. When a height is given, `fit_blocks` shortens section bodies (never the header or command bar) so the frame fits without scrolling, keeping `FRAME_RESERVE` lines free for the note and prompt.

sections.title: Per-section rendering
sections.explanation: `render_section` is one large match over `Section`, building quota (shown as percent left), usage, terminals, budgets, inbox, system and messages blocks. Empty states print helpful hints such as running `agm scan` or `agm hook install`.

sections.title: Sanitising and truncation
sections.explanation: `sanitize_one_line` strips CSI, OSC and other escape sequences and control characters from untrusted text so messages cannot inject terminal codes. `one_line` and `bounded_styled_line` truncate by display width while preserving styling.

sections.title: TUI command parser
sections.explanation: `TuiCmd` enumerates commands, and `TUI_COMMANDS` pairs each full name with a one-letter alias and usage text. Helpers split kinds and quoted tokens and parse `done` filters. `parse_command` maps a line to a `TuiCmd`; empty input means refresh, and missing arguments return usage errors.

src/tui.rs.overview: The interactive `agm tui` binary-side loop: it repaints the dashboard from dashboard.rs on a timer and reads typed commands from a stdin thread. It refuses to run for non-humans and requires a `y` confirmation for kill, interrupt and cleanup. It sits on top of dashboard.rs in the Reporting, TUI and Dashboard tour step.

sections.title: Constants and terminal size
sections.explanation: The header explains the design: no heavy TUI library, typed commands instead of keybindings. `CLEAR_ALL` clears screen and scrollback while staying on the normal screen. `console_size` has separate cfg-specific implementations (env overrides and platform calls) so pane width is known on each OS. `needs_redraw` avoids repainting an identical frame.

sections.title: View persistence and notes
sections.explanation: `load_view` restores the sections chosen with `view` from the `tui_view` setting, falling back to `Section::DEFAULT`. `view_names` and `confirmation_note` format short UI strings.

sections.title: render_frame
sections.explanation: Appends the optional manual-cleanup list and the status note to the rendered dashboard, then builds a single write: cursor home, each line bounded and followed by erase-to-end-of-line, and finally erase-below plus the `agm>` prompt. Doing it in one string reduces flicker.

sections.title: run: setup and caller check
sections.explanation: Spawns a thread that forwards stdin lines over an mpsc channel so the loop can use `recv_timeout`.
