It identifies the caller once via `detect_caller` and bails unless it is a human on a TTY (fail-closed). It starts a background backfill thread with its own `Store` when history coverage is missing, because the SQLite connection is not `Sync`.

sections.title: Render loop
sections.explanation: Each iteration scans for new log data, builds a snapshot and samples system stats, renders, and writes only if the frame changed or input just happened. It then waits for a line up to `refresh` seconds; a timeout just repaints, and a disconnected channel ends the program.

sections.title: Confirmations
sections.explanation: Two pending states are handled before command parsing: a selected cleanup batch and a pending kill or interrupt. Only a line of `y` re-issues the action with `confirmed: true`; anything else cancels. This keeps destructive actions behind an explicit second step.

sections.title: Command dispatch
sections.explanation: Matches the parsed `TuiCmd`: quit, refresh, cleanup selection and listing, kill/interrupt (which stage `pending`), reply, send, done with filters, policy toggle and view get or set. Results become coloured notes shown on the next frame.

sections.title: Unit tests
sections.explanation: Tests cover repaint-only-on-change, the clear sequence, stripping untrusted escapes from notes, and the confirmation instruction preceding long action details.

tests/common/mod.rs.overview: Shared test support: a recording fake of the `Hc` trait (the herdr-core client) so integration tests can exercise actions, rotation and MCP without a real herdr. It is the fake client the Tests and Fixtures tour step refers to.

sections.title: FakeHc state
sections.explanation: `#![allow(dead_code)]` is needed because each test binary uses only part of this module. `FakeHc` records calls in a `RefCell<Vec<String>>` and has knobs: `fail_send`, `apps`, `fail_get`, canned `get_responses`, and `missing_sh_for` to simulate a missing shell on Windows.

sections.title: Read-style methods
sections.explanation: `templates` returns one fixed `worker-mid` template, `ls` is empty, and `get` returns a canned response, a synthetic status with the configured app, or a bare address, or fails with `not_found`.

sections.title: Recording write methods
sections.explanation: `send`, `run`, `kill` and `interrupt` append a readable string to `calls`, which tests assert on (for example that no `kill` happened). `run` can return a spawn failure and otherwise returns a fixed live terminal `t99`.

tests/rotation_test.rs.overview: The heavy integration suite for context-rotation: when a worker or managed agent fills its context window, agm requests a handoff, waits for a committed handoff file, then kills and respawns a successor. Tests drive `rotation::tick` with fake `Hc`, fake `Git` and an in-memory store. It is one of the heavy rotation suites named in the Tests and Fixtures tour step.

sections.title: Fakes and setup
sections.explanation: `FakeGit` implements the `Git` trait and records `touched_since` queries. `interactive_hc` and `setup` build an in-memory store with a live OpenCode worker `t1` linked to a session at 80% context (380k of 475k tokens). `state` reads the rotation row's state, and `go_idle` simulates a new turn.

sections.title: Core lifecycle tests
sections.explanation: Rotation stays `pending` while the agent works, moves to `requested` and sends a handoff prompt once idle, and finishes `done` only after a new turn plus a commit touching the handoff log. Then it kills `t1` and runs a successor named `w-a-2` in the same cwd. Missing commits or timeouts push the item to the inbox instead.

sections.title: Eligibility and safety
sections.explanation: Tests check that only OpenCode workers rotate automatically, that policy-off disables it, that at `max_workers` the old worker is replaced, and that prechecks (a hard budget already exceeded, or an unknown successor) fail before any kill. That last property protects against losing a session without a replacement.

sections.title: Template and launch resolution
sections.explanation: Many paired tests (plain and `_child`) cover how the successor command is built: a bare opencode uses a prompt flag, a template file beats the program path, and a bad disk fallback is handled. Failed rotations are not retried automatically.

sections.title: Managed Claude and Codex rotation
sections.explanation: Covers early failure without cwd, no handoff while done, managed Claude rotation inheriting its launch spec with no kill, cancellation when context drops below the warn level, Codex linking by tag after the old terminal exits, link timeouts moving to needs-attention, and manual rotate ignoring the warn threshold.

sections.title: Warning thresholds and cwd rules
sections.explanation: Unmanaged Claude and Codex only warn at `ctx_rotate`, catalog-only windows still trigger, and the cwd for the successor comes from the launch spec when present, with fallback to the terminal cwd when the spec is missing or blank.

sections.title: Handoff file and missing brief
sections.explanation: A requested rotation continues once the handoff file is ready even if the old terminal exited. A successor that did not receive its brief becomes needs-attention rather than being respawned, matching the `agm spawn` exit-3 behaviour.

tests/fixtures/claude/real_sanitized.jso.overview: A 400-line Claude Code transcript sanitized by tools/sanitize_fixture.py: all free text is replaced with "lorem" but the structure, ids, timestamps, models and token usage remain. It gives the Claude parser and ingestion tests realistic input in the Tests and Fixtures tour step.

sections.title: Session preamble
sections.explanation: Starts with metadata records (`mode`, `permission-mode`, `atis-latch`, `file-history-snapshot`), then the first user message whose content is "lorem" and whose cwd is `D:\fixture\project`, followed by an `ai-title` and a `tools-used` record. These non-message types test that the parser ignores unknown record kinds.

sections.title: Assistant usage turns
sections.explanation: Assistant records carry `message.usage` with input, cache-creation, cache-read and output token counts plus extra fields (`service_tier`, `iterations`, `speed`). These are what usage and context extraction read; interleaved `user` turns, `ai-title` lines and `system` records exercise turn counting.

sections.title: Long tail of the session
sections.explanation: The rest repeats the same record shapes: 144 assistant, 90 user, 33 `ai-title` and 14 `file-history-delta` among other types, with 144 records containing `usage`. The volume makes it a realistic input for incremental tailing and cursor handling.

tools/sanitize_fixture.py.overview: A small Python CLI that converts a real agent JSONL log into a privacy-safe, bounded fixture without touching the source. It is how fixtures like real_sanitized.jsonl are produced, as noted in the Tests and Fixtures tour step.

sections.title: Allow and deny lists
sections.explanation: `PRIVATE_KEYS` are dropped entirely (encrypted content, account and organization ids). `STRING_KEYS` lists structural string fields (type, role, model, ids, timestamps) that are kept verbatim; every other string becomes "lorem". `DISCARDED_TYPES` names record types removed wholesale.

sections.title: discard_line
sections.explanation: Recursively walks a record and returns true if any nested dict has a discarded type, contains `world_state`, or has a value equal to `api-request-blob`. Whole lines are dropped rather than scrubbed when they could hold bulky or sensitive payloads.

sections.title: sanitize
sections.explanation: Recursively rebuilds dicts without private keys, maps lists element-wise, rewrites any `cwd` to `D:\fixture\project`, and replaces non-whitelisted strings with "lorem". Numbers and booleans pass through, so token counts stay real.

sections.title: CLI main
sections.explanation: Parses input, output and `--max-lines` (default 400), validates them and refuses an output equal to the input. It reads with `utf-8-sig` to tolerate a BOM, skips blank and discarded lines, writes sanitized JSON with LF endings and stops at the line limit.

tests/cli_test.rs.overview: End-to-end tests that run the compiled `agm` binary (via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_agm`) inside a temp sandbox with redirected `AGM_*` environment variables. They cover read commands, budgets, policy, hooks, cleanup, help text, `done`, branch set and get, and the MCP server over stdio. They belong to the Tests and Fixtures tour step.

sections.title: Sandbox helpers
sections.explanation: `sandbox` copies the mini Codex and Claude fixtures into a temp dir shaped like the real log roots, and `agm` runs the binary with `AGM_HOME`, `AGM_CODEX_DIR`, `AGM_CLAUDE_DIR`, `AGM_OPENCODE_DB` and `AGM_AGY_DIR` pointed there, so tests never touch real data. `json` asserts success and parses stdout.

sections.title: Read command tests
sections.explanation: Check `ls`, `cost` (unknown model gives null USD), `quota`, a bad config exiting 1, and `log` returning turns. `agm_env` is a variant that also sets a nonexistent hc binary and removes `HC_TERMINAL_ID`.

sections.title: Send, budget and policy
sections.explanation: Cover sending to the user and the inbox, budget set/ls/rm, policy toggling, replaying a daemon event file then checking that an agent cannot kill Codex, and a statusline hook that never fails.

sections.title: TUI and emergency safety
sections.explanation: `cli_tui_with_piped_stdin_cannot_kill_codex` pipes `p off`, `k t1q`, `y` into `agm tui`, expects exit code 1, and verifies the policy remained enabled, proving the TUI refuses non-TTY callers. Other tests cover emergency commands with broken config, `done` dismissal and rotate refusals.

sections.title: Agy, cost windows and rotation
sections.explanation: Cover Antigravity scan and cost, month window and scan-since options, and managed rotate and cleanup behaviour.

sections.title: Help text and cleanup confirmation
sections.explanation: Cleanup with `--yes` must not touch terminals without human confirmation, and help output for every command is checked to be English with the stop and send warnings preserved.

sections.title: Done filters and branch commands
sections.explanation: Cover bulk and range `done` (blocked items are never auto-closed) and the `branch set/get` round trip, rejection of values without `=` and failure for a missing entry.

sections.title: MCP stdio smoke test
sections.explanation: Spawns `agm mcp`, writes `initialize` and `tools/list` requests, closes stdin and uses a 20-second watchdog so a hang fails the test instead of stalling the suite. It then asserts exactly two stdout lines that each parse as JSON.

AGENTS-TUTORIAL.md.overview: The master harness guide (in Vietnamese, v4.0) for running a team of AI agents: roles and permissions, Ponytail policy, Understand-Anything `.ua/` context, shared memory, budget orchestration through agm, and the release gates. It sits above BOT-CEO.md and the docs in the priority order and is the hub that the harness lint scripts check, per the final tour step.

sections.title: Header and priority order
sections.explanation: Gives the version title and a precedence list: project AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md first, then this tutorial, then BOT-CEO.md and other docs. The 4.0 note records dropping GitNexus in favour of Understand-Anything.

sections.title: Architecture and roles
sections.explanation: An ASCII diagram shows herdr and agm at the top, `.ua/` plus shared memory, the Claude CEO, then Antigravity, Codex and OpenCode workers. The roles table lists each tier's model, core permissions and prohibitions, including reviewer independence and the single Git bot.

sections.title: Ponytail policy
sections.explanation: A per-agent table sets Ponytail levels (CEO lite or off, Codex full, workers abbreviated, never `ultra` by default) and gives the four-line rule block embedded in free worker prompts: scope lock, read and reuse first, no safety cuts, honest reports.

sections.title: Skills and worker tiers
sections.explanation: Points to docs/SKILL-ROUTING.md, sets one workflow plus one domain skill as a default (not a hard cap), separates the three code-review roles and defines the three worker tiers (fast, mid, strong) and OpenCode agent file locations.

sections.title: Context layer and shared memory
sections.explanation: Describes `.ua/` Knowledge Graph usage, the shared memory directories with a permission matrix for who may propose or publish, and report standardization that avoids passing conversation history.

sections.title: Coordination and communication
sections.explanation: Covers execution routing, no self-review, one editing branch per area, the budget rules (quota check with `agm quota --refresh`, 70% warning), `agm send` message codes including English aliases, `BRANCHES.md` writes via `agm branch set`, the spawn exit-3 rule, context rotation and git checks at handoffs.

sections.title: Release gates
sections.explanation: A seven-step ordered pipeline: worktree commit, script or CI audit, one independent reviewer, docs and final report, sequential merge by the Git bot, knowledge publication by the CEO, and user-only release. A note clarifies that the `status: ready` guard does not replace these gates.

sections.title: Embedding and references
sections.explanation: Advises against pasting the whole document into AGENTS.md; instead embed a summary of at most 80 lines with pointers, commands and permission boundaries. Closes with reference links.

docs/SKILL-ROUTING.md.overview: An English guide approved 2026-11-23 that picks a workflow skill per phase, role and work type, layered with Ponytail behaviour and a domain skill. It contains a canonical matrix between HTML comment markers that the lint scripts verify, so editing it affects the harness lint in the final tour step.

sections.title: Intro and three layers
sections.explanation: Defines it as dispatch guidance, not an installer. Behaviour (Ponytail), workflow and domain are independent layers; one workflow plus one domain is a default, not a cap, and final verification must never be dropped. It also links to the context-rotation thresholds.

sections.title: Canonical workflow matrix
sections.explanation: A table between `harness:skill-routing:start/end` markers maps logical phases (discovery, system-design, planning, feature, bugfix, review, audit, docs, verification, mechanical and more) to a primary skill and owner. Lint rejects deleted or weakened rows. The matrix selects workflows, not models.

sections.title: Role boundaries and review jobs
sections.explanation: A table sets Ponytail level and skill boundaries per role. A subsection separates requesting, performing and receiving code review so that none replaces another, and says `ponytail-review` is only a complexity supplement.

sections.title: Domain skills and availability
sections.explanation: Maps task types (Rust, Streamlit, React, databases, document formats) to domain skills. A skill available in Codex is not necessarily available in Claude Code, OpenCode or agy, so the manager must resolve installed IDs and report gaps instead of silently substituting.

sections.title: Task brief and examples
sections.explanation: Keeps a single-line, comma-separated `skills:` field. Three sample briefs (feature, bugfix with review feedback, mechanical) show the fields phase, work_type, ponytail, skills, skill_refs, files_allowed and verify. Completion applies verification-before-completion.

sections.title: Verification and sources
sections.explanation: Says to run `scripts/lint_harness.py` and the unittest discovery, notes these only verify document contracts and not runtime skill discovery, and lists reference links.

docs/HARNESS-LINT.md.overview: Operator guide for the harness linter. It explains how to run scripts/lint_harness.py and the test suite, what each diagnostic code group enforces, and which routing contracts are machine-checked. It is the human-facing counterpart of the two Python scripts in tour step 13.

sections.title: Run commands and exit codes
sections.explanation: Lists the two mandatory handoff commands (lint and unittest discover) and the `--root` and `--format json` options. The default root derives from the script location, so the result does not depend on the working directory. Exit 0 is a pass, 1 means lint errors, 2 means bad CLI arguments, and read errors never count as a pass.

sections.title: Coverage table
sections.explanation: A table maps each code family (ENC, MD, LINK, MODEL, POLICY, SEC, IO) to the gate it enforces. It also states the ignored directories and that code fences are not treated as live links. History under docs/superpowers/ is exempt only from obsolete-model checks, not from Markdown, link or secret checks.

sections.title: Routing contracts
sections.explanation: Describes the `harness:*` marker blocks that must be standalone, ordered and unique outside fences. Canonical assignments live in scripts/harness_routing.py, so changing policy requires updating the contract, the guide and tests together. The contracts are documents, not enforced agents or billing limits.

sections.title: Tests proving rejection
sections.explanation: Stresses that negative tests must actually reject bad input, since positive tests alone prove little. It describes the guardrail example tests that run Bash/CI snippets in temporary Git fixtures, and the skill-routing tests. Missing Git or Bash produces explicit skips that must be reported as unverified.

sections.title: Explicit limitations
sections.explanation: Lists what the checker does not do: full CommonMark parsing, network checks, translation equivalence, and complete secret scanning. It reminds readers that lint protects contract tables but prose still needs human review, and that it does not replace application ESLint or tests.

scripts/lint_harness.py.overview: Entry point of the dependency-free harness linter. It walks the repo for Markdown files, parses each with harness_markdown, applies model ID, link and contract checks from harness_routing, redacts secrets and prints a text or JSON report. It is fail-closed: any traversal, read or missing-document problem becomes an error.

sections.title: Imports and constants
sections.explanation: Imports the Document, Issue and parsing helpers from harness_markdown and the checks from harness_routing. IGNORED lists directories never scanned, and REQUIRED lists documents whose absence is an error. The comment notes docs/ is English-only while the root rule docs stay Vietnamese.

sections.title: Report dataclass
sections.explanation: A small dataclass holding the document count and the issue list. It is serialized with `asdict` for JSON output.

sections.title: Document discovery
sections.explanation: Walks the tree with `os.walk` without following links, reporting traversal errors as IO001 and symlinked directories or files as IO002 rather than silently following them. It prunes ignored and symlinked folders in place and sorts for deterministic output. Each `.md` file is read as UTF-8, with failures reported as IO003, then parsed into a Document.

sections.title: Lint orchestration
sections.explanation: Resolves the root and returns IO004 if it is not a directory, then loads documents and flags missing REQUIRED ones as IO005. For each document it runs model ID checks and link checks, converting unexpected OSError or ValueError into IO006 so failure never passes silently. It then merges contract issues and per-document issues, redacts anything matching SECRET from paths and messages, and sorts the result.

sections.title: CLI main
sections.explanation: Defines `--root` (defaulting to the repository root from `__file__`) and `--format`. JSON mode prints the report as ASCII-safe JSON; text mode prints `path:line: CODE message` followed by a summary. The exit code is 1 if any issue exists, otherwise 0, and argparse itself yields 2 for invalid arguments.

scripts/harness_routing.py.overview: Holds the canonical, reviewable routing contracts and the checks that enforce them. Constants define approved model roles, NVIDIA background models, safety rules and skill routing; functions validate model IDs and the marker-delimited contract tables in the policy docs. Policy changes must be made here deliberately, along with docs and tests.

sections.title: Canonical contracts
sections.explanation: Defines the expected role-to-model maps (ROUTING, BACKGROUND, SAFETY, SKILL_ROUTING) as plain dictionaries so any change shows up in review. CONTRACTS maps each policy doc to the named blocks it must contain. Note the reviewer and strong worker use the Pro model while cheaper roles use Flash, and the auditor is script/CI rather than a model.

sections.title: Model catalog and patterns
sections.explanation: MODELS lists the verified variant suffixes allowed per model ID. MODEL_ID is a regex that finds DeepSeek and NVIDIA identifiers with an optional `#variant`, RETIRED names the obsolete free slug, and SECRET matches common NVIDIA and Anthropic/OpenAI key shapes. Secrets are matched narrowly, so this is not a complete scanner.

sections.title: Model ID and secret check
sections.explanation: Scans each line, reporting SEC001 for credential-like text without echoing it. Archived docs/superpowers/ files skip model checks so history can mention retired IDs. Elsewhere it reports MODEL001 for the retired slug, MODEL004 for the wildcard used as a real selection, MODEL002 for unknown IDs and MODEL003 for variants outside the catalog.

sections.title: Contract block parser
sections.explanation: Finds exactly one standalone start and end marker in the visible (non-fenced) lines, otherwise POLICY001. It validates the 3-column table header and separator (POLICY008), rejects non-table content or wrong column counts (POLICY002), duplicate keys (POLICY003) and mismatched values (POLICY004), and reports missing expected keys (POLICY005). Using `doc.visible` is what stops markers hidden in code examples from counting.

sections.title: Contract checking across docs
sections.explanation: For every document in CONTRACTS it looks up the docs/ path, reporting POLICY006 if the file is missing, then runs each named block check. Because docs/ is English-only there is no bilingual drift comparison.
